_meta.indication: Treatment of hyperphenylalaninemia (HPA) in adult and pediatric patients 1 month of age and older with sepiapterin-responsive phenylketonuria (PKU), used in conjunction with a Phe-restricted diet.

pivotal_trials.design: Two-part trial: Part 1 was a 14-day open-label responsiveness phase; Part 2 was a 6-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase with 1:1 randomization and ascending doses given every 2 weeks (20 mg/kg QD for Weeks 1-2, 40 mg/kg QD for Weeks 3-4, and 60 mg/kg QD for Weeks 5-6).
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric and adult participants aged 1 to 61 years with PKU who were determined to be sepiapterin-responsive.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change in blood Phe levels from baseline to Weeks 5 and 6 in the Part 2 double-blind phase.
pivotal_trials.n: 110 patients randomized and treated in Part 2 (Sepiapterin N=56, Placebo N=54).
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant reduction in mean blood Phe: least squares mean difference -395.87 umol/L (95% CI -463.07, -328.66); blood Phe decreased by 410 umol/L in the sepiapterin group vs 16 umol/L in placebo.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=2% and greater than placebo) were diarrhea, headache, abdominal pain, hypophenylalaninemia, feces discoloration, and oropharyngeal pain. Warnings and precautions include increased bleeding and hypophenylalaninemia.
target_moa: Sepiapterin is a synthetic precursor of BH4, converted via the pterin salvage pathway (sepiapterin reductase and dihydrofolate reductase); BH4 is an essential cofactor that activates phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH), the enzyme deficient in PKU.
modality: Small molecule (synthetic form of endogenous sepiapterin, an oral powder).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; no scientific, technical, or policy issues arose that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion.

basis.text: A Preliminary Breakthrough Therapy Designation Request advice teleconference was held, but the Agency indicated a successful designation would require more information; no breakthrough therapy designation was granted.

citations.quote: the Agency informed PTC that a successful breakthrough therapy designation
request would require more information to show that sepiapterin could provide a substantial improvement over existing therapy (e.g., Kuvan) for the treatment of PKU.

basis.text: A Fast Track designation request was submitted with the IND but was denied on September 22, 2021.

citations.quote: Included with the IND submission was a request for a Fast Track designation, which was denied on September 22, 2021, because the submitted data were not adequate to support the potential to address an unmet medical need in the context of available therapies for PKU.

summary.text: SEPHIENCE was approved via a standard review NDA with Orphan Drug Designation (and rare pediatric disease designation); Fast Track was denied and breakthrough therapy was not granted, and the approval was not an accelerated approval.
